finding_F69_ZERO_SORT_AXES.claim: Airbnb offers no sort control at all. It is the only competitor observed with none.
finding_F69_ZERO_SORT_AXES.method: Full page text swept for 'ordenar', 'ordena por', 'sort', 'clasificar', 'relevancia' — zero matches. Zero <select> elements. Every button and combobox enumerated (22 controls): the only ranking-adjacent control is 'Filtros'. This is a positive sweep across two languages, not a failed selector.
finding_F69_ZERO_SORT_AXES.caveat: The 'Filtros' panel was NOT opened. If a sort lives inside it, this finding narrows to 'no sort on the results surface'. Recorded as a limit on the claim, not a hedge on the sweep.
finding_F69_ZERO_SORT_AXES.why_it_matters: Airbnb gives the traveller filters but not ordering. You accept its ranking or you refine the set. For a first-time traveller that is arguably kinder — fewer decisions — and arguably worse: no recourse if the ranking does not suit you, and no visibility into why it ranked that way. Booking.com offers 11 ways to reorder and explains none of them; Airbnb offers zero and likewise explains nothing.

finding_F70_TOTAL_PRICE_ONLY.claim: Airbnb displays the total price for the stay and never a nightly rate. Every other accommodation competitor observed leads with a nightly figure.
finding_F70_TOTAL_PRICE_ONLY.evidence: Prices render as '203 € en total', '199 € en total', '270 € en total', '244 € en total'. Full page swept for 'por noche', '/ noche', 'noche' — ZERO matches.

comparison.Expedia: '$112.77 per night including taxes' — nightly leads
comparison.Booking.com: nightly rate on cards; total appears at property level
comparison.Airbnb: total only, no nightly figure anywhere on the results surface

finding_F70_TOTAL_PRICE_ONLY.why_it_matters_for_luma: Nightly pricing is the industry's standard way of making a stay look cheaper than it is — the traveller multiplies, and the fees arrive later. Airbnb removes that arithmetic entirely at the point of comparison. For a first-time traveller who does not yet know that a €112 night is really €450, this is the single most useful pricing decision observed in the round, and it costs nothing to adopt.
finding_F70_TOTAL_PRICE_ONLY.note: Some cards show a higher struck-through figure beside the total (238 € / 203 €, 288 € / 199 €), so price anchoring is still present — but anchored TOTAL against TOTAL, not nightly against nightly.

aircover_before_booking_TEST_RESULT.the_claim_under_test: Prior desk research held that AirCover's value is naming the safety net and showing it BEFORE booking rather than after failure.
aircover_before_booking_TEST_RESULT.what_was_found: 'AirCover' does appear in the search results page text — but the two matches are 'AirCover' and 'AirCover para anfitriones' (for hosts), consistent with footer navigation rather than a per-listing reassurance badge.
aircover_before_booking_TEST_RESULT.verdict: PARTIALLY SUPPORTED, and weaker than the claim implies. AirCover is reachable from the results surface; it is NOT surfaced per result at the moment of comparison. Whether it appears on the listing page or in checkout is still UNTESTED — the listing page was not opened.
aircover_before_booking_TEST_RESULT.confidence: Verified for what was searched; the claim itself remains OPEN.
aircover_before_booking_TEST_RESULT.why_recorded_this_way: This is a prior-round claim being re-verified, exactly as the clean-room design intended. It is neither confirmed nor refuted yet, and saying so is the point.

our_product_decision_required: Decision required: show total or nightly? Every competitor except Airbnb leads with nightly. Total-first is unoccupied by four of five accommodation products and directly serves a traveller who cannot yet do the arithmetic in their head.

Decision required: how many ways to reorder? The range observed is 0 to 11 and NONE of the five explains its ranking to the traveller. Both extremes are defensible; the unoccupied position is offering few axes and explaining them.
